17 אלף טיסות בוטלו או התעכבו. תחילה היה חשש שמדובר במתקפת סייבר רחבה במיוחד אך שר התחבורה האמריקאי שון דאפי הסביר בתדרוך לתקשורת בבית הלבן כי מדובר פשוט בתקלת תקשורת שהשפיעה על תקשורת הקשר ונתוני המכ”מ וכי ההחלטה להשבית את כלל הטיסות נבעה מטעמי בטיחות. הדרמה נמשכה 4 שעות בהם שמי ארה”ב היו סגורים.

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in a statement:

“On Thursday, I held an important conversation with Gadi Eisenkot. Gadi and I have known each other for many years, dating back to his tenure as IDF Chief of Staff, and even before that.

This meeting only reinforced my understanding of how essential it is, at this time, to establish a national unity government — a government that includes all parties that support the existence of the State of Israel as the nation-state of the Jewish people, and that will be capable of confronting the enormous and complex security challenges ahead of us.

The Iranian regime, which seeks Israel’s destruction, is once again working to revive its nuclear program. Let me be clear: this murderous regime, which did not hesitate to kill many thousands of its own people, will not hesitate to use nuclear weapons against us.

It will do so the moment it succeeds in resuming uranium enrichment and accelerating the development of nuclear weapons.

We must do everything in our power to continue preventing this, just as we did in Operation Rising Lion and Operation Roaring Lion, when we removed the immediate threat of annihilation hanging over us.

We must eliminate this existential threat once and for all.

A narrow government, or a government dependent on supporters of terrorism, will not be able to meet this enormous challenge. But a national unity government will be able to do so in time, thereby ensuring Israel’s security for many years to come.

A national unity government would answer the longing I hear from so many of you, the citizens of Israel — the longing for national reconciliation, for reconciliation among ourselves.

Because, like me, you understand that at this moment, we must work together:

Elisha Midan alongside Elisaf Peretz, Talik Gvili alongside Shira Shapira — a vast Zionist public joining forces to secure Israel’s future.

Gadi,

Instead of trying to form a fragile and dangerous government that would be incapable of meeting even a fraction of the immense security and national challenges before us, let us do what is necessary:

Let us enter a room, without preconditions, put aside all disagreements and boycotts, and reach agreements for the sake of Israel’s security and future — including on the issue of military conscription, which we can resolve together with representatives of the ultra-Orthodox community.

The appropriate response to those who deliberately walked out during the singing of ‘Hatikvah’ — Israel’s national anthem — is to establish the Government of Hope: a national unity government.”

לפי הדיווח, לאחר פגישתו עם ראש ממשלת קטר הצהיר טראמפ כי המלחמה הסתיימה למעשה מבחינה צבאית וכי הסיכוי לחידוש תקיפות נרחבות נמוך מאוד. אולם כעבור ימים ספורים אמר כי ארה״ב כבר אינה זקוקה להסכם עם איראן, והורה לסגנו ג'יי.די. ואנס, שהיה אחראי בעבר על המשא ומתן עם טהראן, להתמקד בענייני הפנים של ארה״ב.

שני דיפלומטים מהמזרח התיכון מסרו ל-AP כי שינויי העמדות של טראמפ הכניסו את מאמצי התיווך של קטר לחוסר ודאות, במיוחד בניסיון להגיע להסכם זמני לפתיחת מצר הורמוז. לדבריהם, עדיין לא ברור אם טראמפ אכן נסוג מהאפשרות של הסכם או שמדובר בטקטיקה שנועדה להגביר את הלחץ על איראן בעקבות הבחירות.

במקביל, טראמפ מדגיש כי צבא ארה״ב ערוך לחלוטין לפעולה צבאית, ומזהיר כי הפעילות הקשורה למתקני הגרעין של איראן, ובהם המתחם המכונה ״הר המכוש״, נמצאת תחת מעקב וכי ארה״ב לא תהסס לפעול צבאית במידת הצורך.

item.title: [amitseg] In 19th-century America, fire departments were commonly run along political lines. Firefighting services were provided f
item.description:
Open
In 19th-century America, fire departments were commonly run along political lines. Firefighting services were provided first and foremost to supporters of the party that had appointed the firefighters. Black people whose homes caught fire received no assistance. At the time, this seemed perfectly reasonable. A hundred or two hundred years later, this is taught in political science departments as an example of corruption that today seems inconceivable.

But is it really so inconceivable? Two public servants, one currently serving and the other retired, are challenging the assumption that public services in Israel are provided equally, without fear or favoritism.

Boaz Balat, head of the Israel Police’s Intelligence and Investigations Division, said in a recording published this week that case files in Israel are kept in drawers and pulled out when needed to pressure citizens or bring police officers who dared to think differently back into line.

Ayala Hasson, a senior presenter at the Israeli Public Broadcasting Corporation, resigned after being repeatedly forced to apologize on air for remarks she had made elsewhere.

Balat explained that investigations are launched or frozen for improper reasons. Hasson described how broadcasts serve one political side for reasons unrelated to professional considerations.

She received unexpected corroboration: a week earlier, during an election broadcast that hosted exclusively opposition supporters, a sign-language interpreter was suddenly heard speaking to his colleague, unaware that his microphone was live: “Isn’t it strange that there hasn’t been a single representative of the right here all evening?”

Strangely enough, the corporation’s management did not subject him to public humiliation as well.

Broadcasting that caters exclusively to one political camp is no different from medical procedures provided through favoritism to only one sector of society. Investigations used not to pursue justice but as instruments of blackmail are no different from fire departments that refuse to extinguish fires at the homes of people who dared to vote differently.

Are left-wing viewers of the public broadcaster not embarrassed by the fact that one billion shekels a year, funded by all of us, are being spent exclusively for their benefit? How is that different from building a road solely for Democratic Party voters?

Some will say, “Tell us something we don’t know.”

After all, Smotrich has also invested enormous sums in his supporters in Judea and Samaria, and there is hardly any need to elaborate on the subsidies provided to the ultra-Orthodox.

The difference is twofold.

First, these are politicians who openly declare their intentions in advance and are elected on that basis. They are not broadcasting services or law enforcement institutions that pride themselves on being apolitical and impartial.

Second, politicians can be replaced, and their priorities can change along with them.

By contrast, the courts—another institution that provides its services primarily to one side—have used their full authority to block any “political” intervention in precisely those institutions: the Public Broadcasting Corporation and the Ministry of Justice.

This was a reckless form of protection that allowed these institutions to continue blatantly discriminating against enormous segments of the population while cynically invoking the term “public service.”

That is why Hasson’s effective dismissal resonated far beyond the dismal ratings of the public broadcaster’s news programs, and why Balat’s recorded remarks were considered far more credible than Israel’s law enforcement system, whose own credibility is rather low.

In 19th-century America, fire departments were politically affiliated. Firefighting services were provided first and foremost to supporters of the political party that had appointed the firefighters. Balat explained that investigations are initiated or frozen for improper reasons. Hasson described how broadcasts serve one political side for reasons unrelated to professional considerations.

She received unexpected corroboration: A week earlier, during an election broadcast that featured exclusively opposition supporters, a sign-language interpreter was suddenly heard speaking to his colleague, unaware that his microphone was live:

“Isn’t it strange that there hasn’t been a single representative of the right here all evening?”

Strangely enough, the broadcaster’s management did not put him in the stocks as well.

Broadcasting that serves only one side is no different from medical procedures granted through favoritism to only one sector of society. Investigations used not to pursue justice but to blackmail people are no different from fire departments that refuse to extinguish fires at the homes of those who dared to vote differently.

**Aren’t left-wing viewers of the public broadcaster embarrassed that a billion shekels a year of everyone’s tax money is being poured exclusively into serving them? How is that different from building a road exclusively for Democratic Party voters?**

Some will respond, “Well, tell us something we don’t know.”

After all, Smotrich has also invested enormous sums of money in his supporters in Judea and Samaria, and there is hardly any need to elaborate on the subsidies provided to the ultra-Orthodox.

The difference is twofold.

First, we are talking about politicians who openly declare their intentions in advance and are elected on that basis—not broadcasting services and law enforcement agencies that pride themselves on being apolitical and impartial.

Second, politicians can be voted out of office, and their priorities can be replaced along with them.

By contrast, the courts—another institution that provides its services primarily to one side—have gone to extraordinary lengths to block any “political” interference in precisely those institutions: the public broadcasting corporation and the Ministry of Justice.

This was a reckless form of protection that allowed these institutions to continue blatantly discriminating against enormous segments of the population while cynically invoking the term “public service.”

That is why Hasson’s effective ousting resonated far beyond the dismal ratings of the public broadcaster’s news programs, and why Balat’s recorded remarks were regarded as far more credible than Israel’s law enforcement system, whose credibility has sunk to a rather low level.

item.description:

חמאס מאשר: מפקד גדוד רפיח חוסל בסיכול ממוקד:

הזרוע הצבאית של חמאס, גדודי עז א-דין אל-קסאם, הודיעה באופן רשמי על מותו של סמיר מחמוד אבו יונס ("אבו מחמוד"), מפקד גדוד רפיח וחבר המועצה הצבאית הכללית של הארגון, שחוסל אמש (שבת) בתקיפה ממוקדת. 

בהודעת הארגון צוין כי אבו יונס, שהצטרף לשורות חמאס ב-1991 וישב בעבר בכלא הישראלי, התקדם לאורך השנים בשדרת הפיקוד ברפיח והחליף בתפקידו את קודמיו שחוסלו – מחמוד חמדאן וניאל אבו עביד. 

עוד הדגישו בחמאס כי אבו יונס נמנה עם הבכירים שלקחו חלק מרכזי בתכנון ובפיקוח על מתקפת ה-7 באוקטובר, והבטיחו לנקום את מותו.

בסרטון המצורף, בחמאס טוענים כי מחמוד היה ממובילי ירי טיל הקורנט לעבר אוטובוס חיילי צה"ל סמוך לאנדרטת חץ שחור בנובמבר 2018 – אירוע שבו נפצע חייל באורח קשה והצית סבב הסלמה בדרום.
